votes.motion: Adopt Joint Ceremonial Resolution 6 of 2026, recognizing June 19, 2026 as Juneteenth Freedom Day in Salt Lake City.
votes.description: The Council adopted a joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall recognizing June 19, 2026 as Juneteenth Freedom Day in Salt Lake City.

votes.motion: Continue the public hearing on the Ordinance for Indefinite Alleyway Closure in Jefferson Park.
votes.description: The Council continued the public hearing on a proposed ordinance to indefinitely close alleyways within Jefferson Park to a future meeting date of July 14, 2026.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 26 of 2026, approving the remaining items and closing Budget Amendment No. 5 for Fiscal Year 2025-26.
votes.description: The Council adopted the fifth budget amendment for FY2025-26, including funding for new police officers, replacement of aging patrol vehicles, a transport van, and a pass-through of property tax revenue to the Salt Lake City Public Library, among other items.

votes.motion: Approve the appointment of Kate Fairchild and David Quealy as Salt Lake City's Judicial Nominating Commission Members.
votes.description: The Council approved the mayoral appointments of Kate Fairchild and David Quealy to serve on Salt Lake City's Judicial Nominating Commission.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 12 of 2026, to designate an assessment area for economic promotion activities in Sugar House over a three-year period (Sugar House Business District 2027 Special Assessment Area).
votes.description: The Council adopted a Resolution of Intention to designate the Sugar House Business District 2027 Special Assessment Area in the core commercial area of Sugar House, including a secondary assessment for specialty lighting and signage for a three-year period.

votes.motion: Approve the Consent Agenda (setting public hearing dates for Alley Vacation at 567 East Warnock Avenue, Mobile Business Text Amendment, and Capital Improvement Program resolution).
votes.description: The Council approved the consent agenda, which set future public hearing dates for multiple items including an alley vacation, a mobile business text amendment, and the Capital Improvement Program funding allocations.
